newsitem.title: UK: EU Commissioner sees dire results if EMU delayed.
newsitem.headline: EU Commissioner sees dire results if EMU delayed.

text.p: European Union monetary affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Thursday a delay in the move to the single currency would result in turmoil on financial markets.
He also said the delay could also dampen efforts by European governments to introduce tighter financial discipline.
"If we said we would push (EMU) out to say, the year 2000, there would be a fantastic relaxation of effort and fiscal consolidation," De Silguy told journalists.
"There would be turmoil on financial markets and consequences for monetary stability."
De Silguy was in London for a series of talks with officials and businessmen about European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
He added it was out of the question Europe would be split into two parts when the single currency becomes a reality.
"We must have a relationship between the 'ins' and the 'pre-ins'," he said.
